title: Credit & debt
examples: What is the difference between APR and the interest rate?
How does making only the minimum payment affect my total debt?
Are there any strategies to pay off credit card debt faster?

explain.say: Today we are looking at understanding credit and debt.

items: Calculating the impact of minimum payments

draw.text: Credit & Debt: APR and Minimum Payments

explain.say: First we need to understand the Annual Percentage Rate or APR.
The APR shows the yearly cost of borrowing money
Next we look at minimum payments required by lenders.
Making only the minimum payment keeps you in debt longer.
In real life, think about a large appliance purchase on credit.

faq.q: What exactly does APR stand for?
faq.a: APR stands for Annual Percentage Rate. It represents the total yearly cost of borrowing money, including interest.
asks: What is the full name of APR?

faq.q: If I only pay the minimum amount, will I ever pay off the debt?
faq.a: Yes, you will eventually pay it off, but the high interest rates mean it will take much longer and cost you more money overall.
asks: Is it possible to pay off debt with minimum payments?
What happens if I only pay the minimum?

faq.q: Is a high APR always bad for me?
faq.a: Generally, yes. A higher APR means the lender charges you more interest each year on the outstanding balance.
asks: Does APR affect how much I pay?
What does a high APR signal?

faq.q: How much extra money should I pay beyond the minimum?
faq.a: Paying more than the minimum significantly reduces the amount of interest you pay and shortens your repayment timeline.
asks: What is the best payment strategy?
How do I pay off debt faster?

faq.q: Does the minimum payment change if my balance changes?
faq.a: Yes, the minimum payment is calculated based on your current outstanding balance and the lender's specific terms.
asks: How is the minimum payment determined?

facts: APR is the yearly cost of borrowing, expressed as a percentage.
Minimum payments are designed to keep the account active but often lead to overpaying in interest.
Paying more than the minimum payment reduces the principal balance faster.
Lenders use APR to give a comprehensive view of the borrowing cost.

quiz.say: If your APR is 24 percent, what does this represent?

options.show: The yearly cost of borrowing money.
options.say: The yearly cost of borrowing money.

options.show: The amount you must pay monthly.
options.say: The amount you must pay monthly.

options.show: The interest rate for the first month only.
options.say: The interest rate for the first month only.

options.show: The total amount of the original loan.
options.say: The total amount of the original loan.

quiz.why: The APR gives you the total percentage cost of the loan over one full year.

wrong.1: This confuses the annual rate with a fixed monthly installment.
wrong.2: APR covers the entire year, not just the first billing cycle.
wrong.3: The APR is a rate, not the principal amount borrowed.

quiz.say: If you only pay the minimum payment, what happens to your debt?

options.show: You will pay off the debt in exactly one year.
options.say: You will pay off the debt in exactly one year.

options.show: The interest charges stop accumulating immediately.
options.say: The interest charges stop accumulating immediately.

options.show: The interest charges remain high relative to the payment.
options.say: The interest charges remain high relative to the payment.

options.show: The debt decreases by a fixed amount every month.
options.say: The debt decreases by a fixed amount every month.

quiz.why: Because the payment is small, the interest charges consume a large portion of your payment, keeping the debt high.

wrong.0: Minimum payments usually require many years, not just one.
wrong.1: Interest continues to accrue as long as the principal balance is outstanding.
wrong.3: The decrease is not fixed because interest is calculated on the remaining balance.

quiz.say: To pay off debt most efficiently, what is the best strategy?

options.show: Pay the full amount only when I get a raise.
options.say: Pay the full amount only when I get a raise.

options.show: Make payments significantly higher than the minimum required amount.
options.say: Make payments significantly higher than the minimum required amount.

options.show: Only pay the minimum to keep my credit score low.
options.say: Only pay the minimum to keep my credit score low.

options.show: Wait until the interest charges are lower before paying extra.
options.say: Wait until the interest charges are lower before paying extra.

quiz.why: Paying extra money directly reduces the principal, minimizing the amount of interest charged over time.

wrong.0: Waiting for a large sum means paying interest on the full balance for too long.
wrong.2: While keeping accounts open is good, only paying minimums is financially costly.
wrong.3: Waiting allows interest to compound, making the debt larger before you can tackle it.
